newsitem.title: GERMANY: Europe's express freight market starts integrating.
newsitem.headline: Europe's express freight market starts integrating.

text.p: The European express freight market is heading for U.S.-style consolidation and integration as competition increases between public and private operators, a transport expert forecast.

Dr Carl-Stefan Neumann, airline and express sector leader for consultants McKinsey & Co, said post offices, private companies and freight forwarders were all moving into the growing light goods market for guaranteed delivery within a day.
The $30 billion European light goods market was now growing at 11 percent compared to eight percent in the U.S., he told the eighth World Express & Mail conference here.
Deutsche Post AG was market leader with a 10 percent share in 1995 while KPN/TNT had 6.6 percent, UPS 5.2 percent, La Poste 4.8 percent and DHL 4.3 percent.

But market concentration would inevitably come since customers increasingly wanted time-definite delivery with one-stop shopping, customised solutions and supply chain integration at highly competitive prices, Neumann said.
Dutch post and telecoms group KPN now faced the challenge of integrating TNT, which it took over at the start of the year to transform it "from a boutique into a high-volume player".
UPS needed to develop critical mass in Europe while regional operators had to establish international operations, he added.
As a pointer to how market concentration could run, Neumann noted that in the U.S. airfreight market FedEx and UPS had a combined 68 percent share in 1994 against 10 percent in 1975.
Neumann said mature European markets such as Germany, the Netherlands and some Scandinavian countries were growing at 5-10 percent and were entering the integration phase.
Countries such as Britain, France and Italy had growth markets rising at 10-20 percent while eastern Europe was still in a creation phase.
